comments.author: @lgallo0113
comments.text:
Total Nonsense!  The Hungarian (Magyar) language does not originate from the Uralic territories, as often stated in many videos. It was not introduced in the Carpathian basin with the arrival of the 7 Magyar tribes in 895AD, one or two of which may have had some genetic connections with the Ural's (and may have PASSED on some loan words to the local Uralic population, which survived to the present day and explains why there are some common words in the two languages) while four of them came from Mesopotamia and one from central Asia, which was the Megyer (the chief) tribe, hence they had different geographic origins, therefore they can not be considered as a monolithic entity, hence they cannot be assumed to be all of Uralic origins. That's a deliberate misrepresentation of the truth.
 The Magyar language was already spoken in the Carpathian basin at the time the Magyar tribes settled there and even millennia before that, as evidenced by it's connections  to language's such as, Etruscan (as explained by the Italian linguist Mario Alinei), Minnoan,  Pelasg/Ancient Greek (as explained by the US linguist Peter Revesz from the University of Nebraska), as well as Sarmatian, Pannon, Hunnic, Sumerian, Iranian, Turkic, Etc. The roots of the Hungarian language go deep into antiquity before the arrival of the Indo-European languages on the European continent, that is why it is an island in the Indo-European sea . That will be the next major challenge for linguists to discover where that root begins.
 So please STOP the erroneous repetitions about the origins of the Magyar language as being Uralic, when all the evidence proves otherwise.
